name: stri_subset_coll<-
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Replace the strings that contain a collation pattern.
origin.usage: stri_subset_coll(str, pattern, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_collator = NULL) <- value

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector. The result has this length.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Collation patterns. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, replace the strings that do not match. An empty string is then replaced.

arguments.name: opts_collator
arguments.text: NULL, or a named list from stri_opts_collator.
Collator settings passed to stri_opts_collator when any are supplied.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Non-empty character vector written onto the matches, in order.

origin.details: Matching uses ICU StringSearch. At strength 1 in German, ss matches ß. An empty string follows negate and is not searched. A missing pattern keeps the original string. An empty pattern makes that element NA and warns. value is recycled over the matches only. A bad locale warns once.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- `stri_subset_coll<-`(c("\u00df", "b"), "ss", strength = 1, locale = "de", value = "Q")
sentence <- paste0('`stri_subset_coll<-`(c("ß", "b"), "ss", strength=1, locale="de", value="Q") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Replace the strings that contain a collation pattern.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, number, logical, or list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Collation pattern or list of patterns. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, replace the strings that do not match. An empty string is then replaced.

arguments.name: opts_collator
arguments.text: None, or a dict of collator settings.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: Collator settings passed to stri_opts_collator when any are supplied.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings written onto the matches, in order.

translation.details: Matching is stri_subset_coll. At strength 1 in German, ss matches ß. An empty string follows negate and is not searched. A missing pattern keeps the original string. An empty pattern makes that element NA and warns. value is recycled over the matches only. A bad locale warns once. The result is a new list.
translation.value: A list the same length as str.
translation.example:
from stringi.subset import stri_subset_coll_assign
x = stri_subset_coll_assign(["ß", "b"], "ss", value="Q", strength=1, locale="de")
print('`stri_subset_coll<-`(["ß", "b"], "ss", strength=1, locale="de", value="Q") returns ' + ", ".join(x) + ".")
